items.title: feat: formalize Knill Question B on Green eigenvalues
items.body:
Fixes #7256.

Formalizes the negative answer to [Knill v2, Sections 1.4 and 10.2, Question B](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18071v2). The connection matrix is indexed by the actual nonempty faces of the existing downward-closed complex type, and the Green matrix is its inverse. The target concerns algebraic multiplicity at the largest real eigenvalue.

A complete [Lean proof](https://github.com/RhudeJJJJ/formal-conjectures/blob/ff6ef371d4497a3d885da5053b91dd580f3a963c/Proofs/KnillGreenProof.lean#L213) now disproves universal simplicity. The witness is the one-dimensional unfilled triangle, with three vertices, three edges and six nonempty faces. It is connected: the checked lemma `triangle_all_pairs` certifies that every pair of vertices is a face. It is not a flag complex. The proof identifies the actual connection matrix, proves its inverse, gives an exact similarity to three 2-by-2 blocks, computes the characteristic polynomial, bounds the real spectrum and proves multiplicity at least two at `(sqrt 5 - 1) / 2`.

The [written odd-cycle manuscript, 9 August 2026](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33368337/Knill_Intake_Gebendorfer_2026-10-13.zip), supplies the construction; this Lean certificate uses its C3 member. It does not certify exact multiplicity two, a smallest counterexample, the entire odd-cycle family, a flag-complex-only statement, or a spectral-radius assertion. Question C remains separate.

Validation: all three proof files in the [complete proof audit](https://github.com/RhudeJJJJ/formal-conjectures/actions/runs/38910970903/job/117006423852) compiled without warnings. All eight printed declarations use only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`. The full upstream [Build project](https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/actions/runs/38911735444/job/117008993476) passed for head `9d06d6eaf6f13f9116e3586d04fd7e4496ae94a8`.

The long proof stays external under PROOFS.md with an immutable formal_proof link; the repository theorem retains its placeholder and the current `question` attribute. The older isolated replay base omits that annotation only; its mathematical definitions and proposition are unchanged. The module remains in `FormalConjectures.Arxiv.«2601.18071».GreenEigenvalue`.

OpenAI Codex assisted with formalization and validation.

items.title: Erdős 241: the best known upper bound is White's (2/μ₂²)^{1/3}, not Green's (7/2)^{1/3}
items.body:
`FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/241.lean` states, as `erdos_241.variants.upper_bound`, that "the best upper bound known to date is due to Green [Gr01], f(N) ≤ ((7/2)^{1/3} + o(1)) N^{1/3}".

This is out of date. Green's argument gives f(N) ≤ ((2/μ₂²)^{1/3} + o(1)) N^{1/3}, where μ₂² is the infimum of ‖g ∗ g‖₂² over g on [−1/2, 1/2] with ∫g = 1; Green used μ₂² ≥ 4/7. Ethan Patrick White, *An optimal L² autoconvolution inequality*, Canad. Math. Bull. 67 (2024), 108–121 ([doi:10.4153/S0008439523000565](https://doi.org/10.4153/S0008439523000565), [arXiv:2210.16437](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.16437)), proves 0.574636066 ≤ μ₂² ≤ 0.574642912 (Theorem 1) and states the consequence for B₃ sets (Corollary 2). The constant becomes (2/0.574636066)^{1/3} ≈ 1.5155.

I plan to add `erdos_241.variants.upper_bound_white` with this constant, cite [Wh24], and reword the docstring of Green's bound. A pull request follows.

items.title: Formalize Knill Question B; odd cycles refute simple maximal algebraic Green eigenvalue
items.body:
I propose formalizing Oliver Knill's Question B as simplicity of the largest algebraic eigenvalue.

### Source and definitions

O. Knill, *Remarks about Connection and Dirac matrices*, [arXiv:2601.18071v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.18071v2), Sections 1.4 and 10.2.

For a finite nonempty abstract simplicial complex, $L_{\sigma\tau}=1$ when $\sigma\cap\tau\ne\varnothing$, and zero otherwise. Set $g=L^{-1}$. Question B asks whether $g$ always has a unique maximal eigenvalue. This intake concerns the largest algebraic eigenvalue, not the eigenvalue of greatest absolute value. Question C is separate.

### Counterfamily

For the one-dimensional cycle complex $C_n$, with unsigned vertex-edge incidence matrix $B$,

```math
L=\begin{pmatrix}I&B\\B^T&B^TB-I\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
g=\begin{pmatrix}I-BB^T&B\\B^T&-I\end{pmatrix}.
```

For each squared singular value $s$, the positive Green root is $(-s+\sqrt{s^2+4})/2$, which decreases strictly with $s$. On odd cycles the smallest squared singular value occurs in exactly two Fourier modes. Thus the largest algebraic Green eigenvalue has multiplicity exactly two on every odd cycle. On even cycles it is simple and equals 1.

$C_5$ is a connected flag witness with ten simplices. Its exact characteristic polynomial is

```math
(x^2+4x-1)(x^4+3x^3-x^2-3x+1)^2.
```

For the cycle family the spectral-radius eigenvalue is simple; that alternative assertion is not refuted.

### Reproduction

The ZIP contains *Odd Cycles and the Maximal Green Eigenvalue of Connection Matrices* (9 August 2026), source and a dependency-free verifier. Run: python3 verify_knill_question_b.py

The one-edge positive control, even-cycle $C_4$ control and exact $C_5$ target all passed.

This requests statement formalization and review of an attached written resolution. The attachment contains a manuscript and executable checks; it is not a Lean proof or an executed Lean build. Author: Jonas J. Gebendorfer. AI assistance was used in derivations, code, checks and preparation.

[Knill_Intake_Gebendorfer_2026-10-13.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33368337/Knill_Intake_Gebendorfer_2026-10-13.zip)

items.title: feat(ErdosProblems/787): add Erdős Problem 787
items.body:
Adds Erdős Problem 787 (Erdős–Moser): $g(n)$ is the largest $m$ such that every set $A$ of $n$ reals has a subset $B$ with $|B| \geq m$ and $b_1 + b_2 \notin A$ for all distinct $b_1, b_2 \in B$. Estimate $g(n)$.

- Definition: `g G n` for any additive type `G` (the problem takes `G = ℝ`), via the shared `Finset.restrictedSumset`: the condition on `B` is `Disjoint B.restrictedSumset A`. For `G = ℝ` or `ℤ`, the set of such $m$ contains $0$ and is bounded by $n$, so `sSup` is a maximum. API lemmas (proved): `disjoint_restrictedSumset_iff` and `le_g`.
- Open: `erdos_787`, "estimate", as `=Θ[atTop] erdos_787.answer`.
- Solved: Choi's observation that we may assume $A \subset \mathbb{Z}$ (`g ℤ n = g ℝ n`); Klarner $g(n) \gg \log n$; Choi [Ch71] $g(n) \ll n^{2/5+o(1)}$; Sanders [Sa21] $(\log n)^{1+c} \ll g(n)$; Ruzsa [Ru05] $g(n) \leq \exp(O(\sqrt{\log n}))$; Beker [Be25] $(\log n)^{1+1/68+o(1)} \ll g(n)$.
- Notes for reviewers:
  - [Er65, p. 187] and [Er73, p. 130] were checked in the Erdős archive: reals, distinct summands, and the sum is tested against all of $A$, as on the site.
  - The site writes Ruzsa's bound as $g(n) \ll \exp(\sqrt{\log n})$. [Ru05] proves $\exp(O(\sqrt{\log n}))$ (as quoted in [Sa21] and [Be25]), which is what we state.
  - Beker's bound is [Be25, Theorem 1.2]: every $c < 1/68$. [Ch71] and [Ru05] were not accessible to me; their statements follow [Er73], [Sa21] and [Be25].
  - Green's Problem 2 (`FormalConjectures/GreensOpenProblems/2.lean`) asks, for the same function over $\mathbb{Z}$, whether $g(n) \geq (\log n)^{100}$.

Checked with `lake --wfail build 'FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«787»'`.

items.title: fix(GreensOpenProblems/27): `green_27.lower` is solved by Cao–Yuan
items.body:
Closes #6729.

**What changed**

- `green_27.lower` goes from `research open` to `research solved`. Its answer, `green_27.lower.answer`, is `fun p ↦ Real.log p * Real.log (Real.log p)`, and its docstring cites the result.
- A new variant, `green_27.variants.lower_cy26`, states $\log p \log \log p \ll m(p)$ on its own, like `lower_be23` and `previous_lower`.
- The `lowerBest` docstring no longer calls Bedert's bound the best known.
- New reference [CY26].

**Why**

Cao and Yuan ([arXiv:2608.06728](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06728), Theorem 1.1) prove that for every prime $p$, every $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $|A| \ge 2$ and no unique sum satisfies $|A| \ge c_* \log p \log \log p$ for an explicit constant $c_* > 0$. Their $m(p)$ is FC's `m`: representations are unordered pairs, and repetition is allowed.

The answer satisfies both parts of `green_27.lower`:

- `lowerBest =o green_27.lower.answer`, because their ratio is $\sqrt{\log \log \log p} / (\log \log \log \log p \cdot \log \log p)$, which tends to $0$.
- `green_27.lower.answer =O m` is Theorem 1.1.

**Not included**

- `green_27.upper` and `green_27.equivalent` stay open. Cao and Yuan's upper bound (Theorem 1.3) improves only the constant in front of $(\log p)^2$.
- A stronger bound, $m(p) \gg (\log p / \log \log p)^2$, is proved by Xinjie He ([working draft](https://github.com/xinjiegit/ben_27_formalization/blob/f70352964007662e97a810c880abbfea1e2ea262/NUS_edited.tex), with a Lean proof) and by Hou and Yang ([arXiv:2610.09349](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09349)). I proposed it in a separate issue, #6969, so that this PR covers only #6729.

**Notes**

The paper is an arXiv v1 preprint (7 August 2026) and is not yet refereed. It says its main results were checked in Lean 4 but gives no public link, so this PR adds no `formal_proof` attribute. #5535 marked `green_38.lower` solved from arXiv preprints in the same way.

**Checks**

`lake --wfail build 'FormalConjectures.GreensOpenProblems.«27»'` passes, and so does `FormalConjectures.Subsets.FC100SolvedSet2`, the only module that imports this file. From this file it lists only `green_27.variants.lower_be23`, which this PR does not change.

items.title: feat(GreensOpenProblems/64): formalize Ω(p-2) odd infinitude question
items.body:
Formalizes [Green's open problem 64](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.64):

> Do there exist infinitely many primes $p$ for which $p - 2$ has an odd number of prime factors, counted with multiplicity?

## Statement

```lean
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem green_64 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ Odd (Ω (p - 2))}.Infinite
```

where `Ω` is `ArithmeticFunction.cardFactors` (number of prime factors with multiplicity). This mirrors the existing twin-prime style infinitude statements in the repo.

## Test witnesses

Three decidable `category test` lemmas keep the definition honest:

- `green_64_mem_five` / `green_64_mem_seven`: 5 and 7 qualify (for these, `p - 2` is itself prime, so `Ω (p - 2) = 1` is odd).
- `green_64_not_mem_eleven`: 11 does *not* qualify, since `11 - 2 = 9 = 3 ^ 2` gives `Ω 9 = 2`, which is even — showing the condition is non-trivial.

## Verification

- `lake build --wfail 'FormalConjectures.GreensOpenProblems.«64»'` passes clean (linters as errors).
- `#print axioms` on all three test lemmas: `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` only (no `sorryAx`).

Closes #1684.

AI assistance (added 3 Nov 2026): the Lean code, this description and my replies in this thread were written with Claude (Anthropic). I reviewed the changes and ran the build checks locally.

items.title: Add Erdős Problem 748 (the Cameron–Erdős conjecture), link the formal proof
items.body:
Fixes #6349.

### What changed
Adds `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/748.lean` with `f n` (the number of sum-free subsets of `[1, n]`, via the existing `IsSumFree`):
- `erdos_748` (`research solved`, `answer(True)`): the Cameron–Erdős conjecture `f(n) = 2^{(1+o(1)) n/2}`, formalised as `log₂ f(n) / n → 1/2`. Linked to plby/lean-proofs `Erdos748.erdos_748` (Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol; 2 Mathlib-only files).
- Sorry'd variants: the trivial lower bound `2^{⌊n/2⌋} ≤ f(n)`, Green–Sapozhenko's `f(n) ≪ 2^{n/2}`, and the parity-dependent asymptotic `f(n) ∼ c_n 2^{n/2}`.

### How checked
- Rebuilt plby's closure against this repo's Mathlib: `#print axioms Erdos748.erdos_748` → `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`.
- Bridge compiled against the new statement on top of a renamed copy, same axioms:

<details>
<summary>Bridge</summary>

```lean
open Filter Real

namespace Bridge748

lemma isSumFree_iff' (A : Finset ℕ) : IsSumFree (A : Set ℕ) ↔ Erdos748Plby.IsSumFree A := by
  rw [_root_.isSumFree_iff]
  simp only [Finset.mem_coe, Erdos748Plby.IsSumFree]
  exact ⟨fun h b c hb hc => h b hb c hc, fun h b hb c hc => h hb hc⟩

lemma f_eq (n : ℕ) : Erdos748.f n = Erdos748Plby.sumFreeCount n := by
  classical
  unfold Erdos748.f Erdos748Plby.sumFreeCount
  have : ((Finset.Icc 1 n).powerset.filter fun A : Finset ℕ ↦ IsSumFree (A : Set ℕ)) =
      Erdos748Plby.sumFreeSubsets n := by
    ext A
    rw [Erdos748Plby.mem_sumFreeSubsets_iff, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_powerset,
      isSumFree_iff']
  rw [this]

theorem erdos_748_bridge : type_of% Erdos748.erdos_748 := by
  show True ↔ _
  simp only [true_iff, f_eq]
  exact Erdos748Plby.erdos_748

#print axioms Erdos748Plby.erdos_748
#print axioms erdos_748_bridge

end Bridge748
```
</details>

- `lake --wfail build FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«748»` passes.

items.title: GreensOpenProblems/27: record the near-quadratic lower bound for `m`
items.body:
After #6968, `FormalConjectures/GreensOpenProblems/27.lean` records Cao and Yuan's lower bound $m(p) \gg \log p \log \log p$. Two works prove the stronger bound $m(p) \gg (\log p / \log \log p)^2$:

- **Xinjie He**, "A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums", [working draft](https://github.com/xinjiegit/ben_27_formalization/blob/f70352964007662e97a810c880abbfea1e2ea262/NUS_edited.tex) dated 21 July 2026, Theorem 1.2. Its Lean 4 proof is [`NUS.m_lower_bound`](https://github.com/xinjiegit/ben_27_formalization/blob/f70352964007662e97a810c880abbfea1e2ea262/NUSLean/Main.lean#L164), registered as [PALOMAR-2026-08-18-000003](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-08-18-000003&version=1). The repository says that the Lean proof was developed with AI assistance under human direction. It does not claim independent human peer review of the Lean development.
- **Jianfeng Hou and Kai Yang**, "A near-quadratic lower bound for sets with no unique sums", [arXiv:2610.09349](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09349), posted 7 October 2026. Theorem 1.1 gives $m(p) \ge 2^{-80} (\log p / \log \log p)^2$ for every prime $p \ge 64$.

Both works define $m(p)$ as FC's `m` does: representations are unordered pairs, and repetition is allowed.

With `green_27.variants.upper_be23`, this gives $m(p) = (\log p)^{2 + o(1)}$. The exact order of $m(p)$ is still open, so `green_27.upper` and `green_27.equivalent` stay open.

**Suggested change:** add both references, mention the bound in the `green_27.lower` docstring, and add a variant `green_27.variants.lower_he26_hy26` with a `formal_proof` link to He's theorem. The answer of `green_27.lower` stays as it is, since it already beats `lowerBest`. #5535 did the same for `green_38.lower`. I will open a PR for this.

*AI assistance: I used Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) to find these sources and draft this issue.*

items.title: fix(GreensOpenProblems/54): use Minkowski sumsets, not scalar dilations
items.body:
`green_54` required `C ⊆ (10 : ℝ) • K` and `green_54_known_case` used `C ⊆ (2 : ℝ) • K` — scalar dilations `{r • x | x ∈ K}`. Green's Problem 54 (Talagrand's convexity question) takes the tenfold Minkowski sum `K + ⋯ + K`, and the known negative case concerns `K + K`. Since `K` is balanced but not assumed convex, the dilation and the sumset are different sets, so both statements were about the wrong object.

**Change:** replace the dilations by pointwise sumsets: `(10 : ℕ) • K` (the 10-fold sumset under `open scoped Pointwise`) in `green_54` and `K + K` in `green_54_known_case`. Docstrings and references updated; a note explains the `n • K` notation.

**Checked:** `lake --wfail build FormalConjectures.GreensOpenProblems.«54»` passes with no warnings.

Reviewer judgement call: `green_54` is additionally marked `research solved` with `answer(True)`, citing the 2026 Hua–Song–Tudose preprint (arXiv:2605.10908), which proves that `γ_n(A) > 5/6` implies `3(A + A + A)` contains a symmetric convex body `C` with `γ_n(C) ≥ 1/4`, uniformly in `n`. Please check that the preprint's finite-dimensional, uniform-in-`n` result is accepted as settling the infinite-dimensional formulation used here; if not, the status change can be reverted independently of the sumset fix.

Fixes #5683

items.title: fix(GreensOpenProblems/37): replace the unconstrained O/o variants
items.body:
`green_37_bigO` and `green_37_littleO` asked for some `f` with `m(·, k) =O[atTop] f`
resp. `=o[atTop] f` and constrained `f` in no other way, so both were settled for every `k`
by an elementary answer: the interval `{0, …, kN}` is an AP cover, giving `m N k ≤ kN + 1`,
so `answer(fun N ↦ (N : ℝ))` and `answer(fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ 2)` work. Green's Problem 37 asks
for the smallest such cover, and its comments state the substantive conjecture
`F_k(N) ≫_k N^(1 - c_k)` with `c_k → 0` as `k → ∞`.

**Change:** the two unconstrained variants are replaced by the mathematics they were missing.
`m_le_mul_add_one` (`@[category API]`) is the elementary bound `m N k ≤ k * N + 1`, proved from
the cover `{0, …, kN}`. `green_37_lower_bound` (`@[category research open]`) states Green's
conjecture: there is `c : ℕ → ℝ` with `c → 0` such that for every `k > 0`,
`(fun N ↦ (N : ℝ) ^ (1 - c k)) =O[atTop] fun N ↦ (m N k : ℝ)`. `green_37`,
`green_37_asymptotic` and `green_37_theta` are unchanged; the last already asks for the
growth of `m(·, k)` up to constants.

**Checked:** `lake --wfail build FormalConjectures.GreensOpenProblems.«37»` —
`Build completed successfully`, no warnings.

The lower bound is quantified over `k > 0` only: `m N 0 = 0`, and `=O` against the zero
function would be false. No positivity is imposed on `c`, matching the source, which states
only `c_k → 0`.

Fixes #6476

items.title: fix(GreensOpenProblems/14): `W_3_29_eq` and `W_3_30_eq` are false

labels.name: solution found
labels.description: should be used when changing the status of a problem from `research open` to `research solved`

items.body:
Set `W_3_29_eq` and `W_3_30_eq` to `answer(False)` and mark both `research solved`.

**Why:** Chowdhury, Codel and Heule, *A linear weight transfer rule for local search*, NFM 2023 ([PDF](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~mheule/publications/NFM23.pdf), Section 6.3), solved the satisfiable instances `Green-29-868-SAT` and `Green-30-903-SAT`, i.e. found 2-colourings of $\{1,\ldots,868\}$ and $\{1,\ldots,903\}$ with no red 3-AP and no blue 29-AP (resp. 30-AP). They state the resulting bounds $W(2;3,29) \ge 869$ and $W(2;3,30) \ge 904$, refuting the values $868$ and $903$ conjectured in [AKS14, Table 2].

In the formalisation `W k r` is the least $N$ in `mixedMonoAPGuaranteeSet k r`, and that set is upward closed, so $868 \notin$ the set gives `W 3 29 ≠ 868`; likewise for 30.

The existing `W_3_29_lower` and `W_3_30_lower` ($\ge 868$, $\ge 903$) remain correct and are left unchanged; stronger lower-bound statements could be added separately. [CCH23] is added to the module docstring.

Fixes #6728.

items.title: fix(GreensOpenProblems/16,24,35,37): answer slots depend on binders
items.body:
Several `answer(sorry)` slots in `GreensOpenProblems` were closed terms placed under a quantifier whose value they must depend on. Under the `with_auxiliary` reading (the answer is a top-level constant) each such statement is false: `green_24` asserts that `max013AffineTranslates` is constant, `green_16` that the maximal solution-free size is independent of `N`, `green_37` that the least cover size is independent of `N` and `k`, and `green_37_asymptotic` / `green_37_theta` that one function of `N` serves every `k` (`m N 0 = 0` while `m N 1 = 1`). In `35.lean` the slots were inert: the improvement conjuncts spoke about `c`, not the answer.

**Change** (per file)

- `24.lean`: `green_24` asks for a function `ℕ → ℕ`, applied to `n`.
- `16.lean`: `green_16` asks for a function `ℕ → ℕ`, applied to `N`.
- `37.lean`: `green_37` asks for `ℕ → ℕ → ℕ` applied to `N k`; `green_37_asymptotic` and `green_37_theta` ask for `ℕ → ℕ → ℝ` applied to `k` (docstrings updated). `green_37_bigO` / `green_37_littleO` are untouched; they admit a closed answer and are handled in #4943.
- `35.lean`: `green_35.lower` now requires the answer `lb` (not `c`) to beat the known values at `p = 2` or `p = ∞`; `green_35.upper` now asks to beat the best-known `0.75265`. The `c(∞)` upper bounds are corrected: the cited sources state their constants for functions supported on `[-1/4, 1/4]`, and rescaling to `[0, 1]` halves them (as Green notes for [CS17]: `1.28 → 0.64`). [MV10] proves `1.50972…`, i.e. `c ∞ ≤ 0.7549`, not `0.7505` (Green's `0.75049…` is a misprint of `0.7549…`); `variants.c_inf_upper` is corrected accordingly. The AlphaEvolve bound from Green's 2025 update ([AE25], `1.5053`, i.e. `c ∞ ≤ 0.75265`; Green's `0.75026` is likewise a misprint) is added as `variants.c_inf_upper_ae25` and used as the threshold in `green_35.upper`, which therefore stays open.
- `41.lean`: not changed here; `green_41` is covered by #5757 (branch `fix/issue-5680`).
